answer: No need for a record-at-a-time path. A 3-minute SLA is far above micro-batch latency, so use micro-batch on the cluster the operations group already runs. Micro-batch latency is roughly trigger interval plus batch run time, with p99 near the full trigger plus the slowest run. A 30 second trigger gives p99 around 40 seconds, under 180 seconds. The decision has two steps: first, does p99 fit under the SLA given the trigger floor (it does, with room); second, when both engines meet the SLA, the team decides. Shared functions, deploy pipeline and on-call skills favor micro-batch. Record-at-a-time would only be justified by a sub-2-second-type SLA that no trigger can meet. Source: pa_pattern_batch_or_stream_intermediate.md, L325-385.
